acronymsQuiz.name: CompTIA A+ Acronyms Quiz
acronymsQuiz.description: Acronyms quiz covering CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) exam domains

questions.stem: Which main hardware component of a computer is responsible for executing instructions and processing data?
questions.explanation: CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the main hardware component responsible for executing instructions and processing data in a computer.

questions.stem: A cyberattack focused on making a website, service, or network unavailable to users by overloading it with traffic or malicious requests is referred to as:
questions.explanation: DoS (Denial of Service) is a cyberattack that aims to make a website, service, or network unavailable to legitimate users by overwhelming it with excessive traffic or malicious requests.

questions.stem: What is the name of a network protocol that secures web traffic via SSL/TLS encryption?
questions.explanation: HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure) uses SSL/TLS encryption to secure web traffic between a browser and server, protecting data integrity and confidentiality.

questions.stem: A legal contract between the holder of confidential information and another person to whom that information is disclosed restricting that other person from disclosing the confidential information to any other party is known as:
questions.explanation: NDA (Non-Disclosure Agreement) is a legal contract that restricts one or more parties from disclosing confidential information shared between them to any outside party.

questions.stem: Which wireless technology enables identification and tracking of tags attached to objects?
questions.explanation: RFID (Radio-Frequency Identification) uses electromagnetic fields to automatically identify and track tags attached to objects, enabling wireless identification at varying distances.

questions.stem: A type of cryptographic network protocol for secure data communication, remote command-line login, remote command execution, and other secure network services between two networked computers is called:
questions.explanation: SSH (Secure Shell) is a cryptographic network protocol that provides encrypted communication for secure remote login, command execution, and other network services between two networked computers.

questions.stem: Which acronym refers to the network name visible to users when they look for available Wi-Fi networks?
questions.explanation: SSID (Service Set Identifier) is the human-readable name assigned to a wireless network that users see when scanning for available Wi-Fi connections.

questions.stem: What is the common term for a group of protocols used to carry voice data over a packet-switched network?
questions.explanation: VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) is a group of technologies and protocols that enable voice communications and multimedia sessions to be transmitted over packet-switched IP networks instead of traditional phone lines.

questions.stem: A computer network connecting multiple LANs over an area of a city is referred to as:
questions.explanation: MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) is a computer network that spans a city or large campus, interconnecting multiple LANs across a metropolitan area.

questions.stem: LDAP is an example of:
questions.explanation: LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) is a directory access protocol used to query and modify directory services such as Active Directory, providing a centralized way to manage user accounts and network resources.

questions.stem: What is the name of a network layer protocol that specifies the format of packets and addressing scheme in network communications?
questions.explanation: IP (Internet Protocol) is a network layer protocol that defines the format of data packets and the addressing scheme (IPv4/IPv6) used to route traffic across interconnected networks.

questions.stem: Which digital media interface provides the capability for transmission of both video and audio data?
questions.explanation: HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface) is a digital audio/video interface standard capable of transmitting both high-definition video and multi-channel audio through a single cable.

questions.stem: Which of the following acronyms refers to a set of rules that specify which users or system processes are granted access to objects as well as what operations are allowed on a given object?
questions.explanation: ACL (Access Control List) is a set of rules that specifies which users or system processes are granted or denied access to objects, and what operations are permitted on those objects.

questions.stem: TCP is a connection-oriented network protocol using a three-way handshake which is a set of initial steps required for establishing network connection. TCP supports retransmission of lost packets, flow control (managing the amount of data that is being sent), and sequencing (rearranging packets that arrived out of order). Example applications of TCP include transmission of text and image data.
questions.explanation: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is a connection-oriented transport layer protocol that uses a three-way handshake to establish connections and provides reliable data delivery through retransmission, flow control, and packet sequencing.

questions.stem: A type of smart card used in mobile phones to identify the client is known as:
questions.explanation: SIM (Subscriber Identity Module) is a smart card inserted into mobile phones that stores the subscriber's identity, phone number, and authentication data to identify the device on a cellular network.

questions.stem: Which part of the AAA security architecture ensures that users are who they claim to be, typically through credentials like passwords or biometrics?
questions.explanation: AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting) is a security framework. Authentication is the first component, which verifies users are who they claim to be through credentials such as passwords, tokens, or biometrics.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a system containing mappings of domain names to various types of data, such as numerical IP addresses?
questions.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) is a hierarchical naming system that translates human-readable domain names (e.g., example.com) into numerical IP addresses that computers use to locate each other on a network.

questions.stem: Which of the following devices combines printing, scanning, copying, and often faxing into a single unit? (Select the best answer)
questions.explanation: MFP (Multifunction Printer) is a device that combines printing, scanning, copying, and often faxing capabilities into a single unit, reducing the need for multiple standalone devices.

questions.stem: An internal hardware component that converts electrical power from an outlet into usable power for a computer’s internal parts is called:
questions.explanation: PSU (Power Supply Unit) is an internal hardware component that converts alternating current (AC) power from a wall outlet into regulated direct current (DC) power used by a computer's internal components.

questions.stem: Which type of software acts as an intermediary between users and computer hardware, enabling both system operations and application execution?
questions.explanation: OS (Operating System) is system software that acts as an intermediary between users and computer hardware, managing resources, running applications, and providing a user interface.

questions.stem: Which of the acronyms listed below refers to a network protocol for secure file transfer over SSH?
questions.explanation: SFTP (Secure File Transfer Protocol) is a network protocol that provides secure file transfer capabilities over an SSH connection, encrypting both commands and data in transit.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of S.M.A.R.T. in a storage media drive?
questions.explanation: S.M.A.R.T. (Self-Monitoring, Analysis, and Reporting Technology) is a monitoring system built into storage drives (HDDs and SSDs) that detects and reports indicators of drive reliability, predicting impending hardware failures.
options: Automatic correction of detected drive errors
Real-time monitoring and regulation of power consumption
Prediction and reporting of impending drive failures
correctAnswer: Prediction and reporting of impending drive failures

questions.stem: A solution that allows to supply electricity over standard Ethernet cables is referred to as:
questions.explanation: PoE (Power over Ethernet) is a technology that delivers electrical power along with data over standard Ethernet cabling, eliminating the need for separate power supplies for devices like IP cameras and wireless access points.

questions.stem: IMAP is used for:
questions.explanation: IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) is an email retrieval protocol that allows a client to access and manage email messages stored on a remote mail server, keeping messages synchronized across multiple devices.
options: Translating domain names into IP addresses
Retrieving email messages from a mail server
correctAnswer: Retrieving email messages from a mail server

questions.stem: A dedicated data storage solution that combines multiple disk drive components into a single logical unit to increase volume size, performance, or reliability is known as:
questions.explanation: RAID (Redundant Array of Independent Disks) is a data storage technology that combines multiple physical disk drives into a single logical unit to improve performance, increase storage capacity, or provide data redundancy.

questions.stem: A computer's primary storage media used for quick access to working data and code is known as:
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is a computer's volatile primary storage that provides fast read/write access to data and program instructions currently in use by the CPU.

questions.stem: Which of the following answers refers to a unique 48-bit address assigned to every network adapter?
questions.explanation: MAC (Media Access Control) address is a unique 48-bit hardware identifier permanently assigned to a network interface controller (NIC), used for communication within a network segment at the data link layer.

questions.stem: What is the function of FTP?
questions.explanation: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is a standard network protocol used for transferring files between a client and a server over a TCP/IP network.

questions.stem: Which of the terms listed below is used to describe a mechanical data storage medium type that relies on magnetic plates and moving parts for data storage and retrieval?
questions.explanation: HDD (Hard Disk Drive) is a mechanical data storage device that uses spinning magnetic platters and read/write heads to store and retrieve digital data.

questions.stem: What is the name of a hardware device that allows for administering multiple hosts with the use of a single mouse, keyboard, and computer screen?
questions.explanation: KVM (Keyboard, Video, Mouse) switch is a hardware device that allows a user to control multiple computers from a single keyboard, monitor, and mouse setup.

questions.stem: Which technology uses infrared light waves to enable short-range wireless communication, often found in remote controls?
questions.explanation: IR (Infrared) is a wireless communication technology that uses infrared light waves for short-range data transmission, commonly found in remote controls and some legacy device interfaces.

questions.stem: PCIe is a high-speed, serial expansion bus designed as a replacement for PCI, PCI-X, and AGP standards.
questions.explanation: PCIe (Peripheral Component Interconnect Express) is a high-speed serial expansion bus standard that replaced older PCI, PCI-X, and AGP interfaces, providing faster data transfer rates for expansion cards like GPUs and NVMe SSDs.

questions.stem: A type of firmware interface designed as a replacement for traditional BIOS is called:
questions.explanation: UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) is a modern firmware interface that replaces the traditional BIOS, offering faster boot times, support for larger drives, a graphical interface, and enhanced security features like Secure Boot.

questions.stem: Which of the following acronyms refers to a general-purpose computing device designed for individual use?
questions.explanation: PC (Personal Computer) is a general-purpose computing device designed for individual use, typically consisting of a CPU, memory, storage, and input/output peripherals.

questions.stem: What is the most common motherboard form factor used in desktop PCs?
questions.explanation: ATX (Advanced Technology eXtended) is the most common motherboard form factor for desktop PCs, defining standardized board dimensions, mounting hole locations, and power connector specifications.

questions.stem: Which of the cryptographic algorithms listed below is the least vulnerable to attacks?
questions.explanation: AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) is a symmetric-key encryption algorithm widely adopted as the most secure standard for encrypting electronic data, using key sizes of 128, 192, or 256 bits.

questions.stem: A type of limited-range computer network used for data transmission among various types of personal devices is referred to as:
questions.explanation: PAN (Personal Area Network) is a short-range computer network used for communication among personal devices such as smartphones, tablets, and laptops, typically within a range of a few meters using Bluetooth or similar technologies.

questions.stem: Which type of firmware performs initial hardware checks after the computer is powered on?
questions.explanation: BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) is firmware stored on the motherboard that performs the POST (Power-On Self-Test) and initializes hardware components during the boot process before handing control to the operating system.

questions.stem: A mobile device deployment model that allows employees to use private mobile devices for accessing the company's restricted data and applications is known as:
questions.explanation: BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) is a mobile device deployment model that allows employees to use their personal devices (smartphones, laptops, tablets) to access company data, applications, and network resources.

questions.stem: Which of the following terms refers to a common PnP interface that allows a PC to communicate with peripherals and other devices?
questions.explanation: USB (Universal Serial Bus) is a widely used plug-and-play interface standard that enables PCs to communicate with peripherals and other devices, providing both data transfer and power delivery through a single connection.

questions.stem: Antistatic bags, antistatic wrist straps, and ground mats are all countermeasures used to protect computer and communications equipment components against:
questions.explanation: ESD (Electrostatic Discharge) is the sudden flow of static electricity between two objects with different electrical potentials, which can damage sensitive electronic components. Antistatic bags, wrist straps, and ground mats are used as protective countermeasures.

questions.stem: APIPA allows a Windows host to self-configure an IPv4 address and subnet mask when a DHCP server is unavailable. APIPA uses the address block range from 169.254.0.0 to 169.254.255.255. APIPA-assigned addresses are valid only for communication within the network segment to which the host is connected. A host with an APIPA-assigned address cannot connect to the Internet.
questions.explanation: APIPA (Automatic Private IP Addressing) is a Windows feature that allows a host to automatically self-assign an IP address in the 169.254.0.0/16 range when no DHCP server is available, enabling local network communication only.

questions.stem: In the AAA security architecture, the process of tracking user activity and resource usage for reporting or billing is called:
questions.explanation: In the AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting) security framework, Accounting is the process of tracking and logging user activity, resource usage, and session data for reporting, auditing, or billing purposes.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to one of the major CPU manufacturers for PCs?
questions.explanation: AMD (Advanced Micro Devices) is one of the two major CPU manufacturers for PCs (alongside Intel), producing processors, GPUs, and other semiconductor products.

questions.stem: Which hardware component in a PC stores BIOS/UEFI configuration settings and retains them using battery power?
questions.explanation: CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor) refers to a small amount of battery-backed memory on the motherboard that stores BIOS/UEFI configuration settings such as date/time, boot order, and hardware parameters.

questions.stem: Which of the following acronyms refers to an agreement that specifies performance requirements for a vendor?
questions.explanation: SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a contract between a service provider and a customer that specifies measurable performance requirements, expected service levels, and remedies if those targets are not met.

questions.stem: A type of network connecting computers within a small geographical area such as a building or group of buildings is referred to as:
questions.explanation: LAN (Local Area Network) is a computer network that connects devices within a limited geographical area such as a home, office, building, or campus, typically using Ethernet or Wi-Fi.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a display technology most commonly used in modern laptops?
questions.explanation: LCD (Liquid Crystal Display) is a flat-panel display technology that uses liquid crystals modulated by electric current to produce images, and is the most commonly used display type in modern laptops and monitors.

questions.stem: Which cloud service model would provide the best solution for a web developer intending to create a web app?
questions.explanation: PaaS (Platform as a Service) is a cloud computing service model that provides a platform with development tools, runtime environments, and infrastructure, allowing developers to build, test, and deploy applications without managing the underlying hardware.

questions.stem: Which network protocol is used to retrieve content from a web server?
questions.explanation: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is the foundational application-layer protocol used by web browsers to request and retrieve content (web pages, images, etc.) from web servers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an MS Windows component that enables encryption of individual files?
questions.explanation: EFS (Encrypting File System) is a Windows component that provides file-level encryption, allowing users to encrypt individual files and folders on NTFS volumes to protect sensitive data.

questions.stem: Which technology allows a physical network to be divided into multiple logical broadcast domains for better segmentation and management?
questions.explanation: VLAN (Virtual Local Area Network) is a network technology that logically segments a physical network into multiple isolated broadcast domains, improving security, performance, and network management without requiring separate physical infrastructure.

questions.stem: Which MFP feature optimizes the processing of multi-page documents?
questions.explanation: ADF (Automatic Document Feeder) is a feature on multifunction printers and scanners that automatically feeds multiple pages for scanning, copying, or faxing without requiring manual placement of each page.

questions.stem: A cloud computing service model offering remote access to applications based on monthly or annual subscription fee is referred to as:
questions.explanation: SaaS (Software as a Service) is a cloud computing service model in which applications are hosted by a provider and made available to users over the internet, typically on a subscription basis.

questions.stem: Which of the acronyms listed below refers to a network of interconnected devices equipped with sensors (such as wearable tech or home automation devices) that can interact with each other to perform various tasks and functions?
questions.explanation: IoT (Internet of Things) refers to a network of interconnected physical devices equipped with sensors, software, and network connectivity that collect and exchange data, enabling automation and remote monitoring.

questions.stem: Which DNS database record maps a domain name to a list of mail servers for that domain?
questions.explanation: MX (Mail Exchanger) is a type of DNS record that specifies the mail servers responsible for receiving email messages on behalf of a domain and their priority order.

questions.stem: A network protocol providing an alternative solution to the manual allocation of IP addresses is known as:
questions.explanation: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) is a network protocol that automatically assigns IP addresses, subnet masks, default gateways, and other network configuration parameters to devices, eliminating the need for manual IP configuration.

questions.stem: Which of the following terms refers to an older hardware bus standard, now largely deprecated, used to connect peripheral devices directly to a computer’s motherboard?
questions.explanation: PCI (Peripheral Component Interconnect) is an older hardware bus standard used to connect expansion cards (such as network adapters and sound cards) to a motherboard, now largely deprecated in favor of PCIe.

questions.stem: The term "SMS" is used in reference to:
questions.explanation: SMS (Short Message Service) is a text messaging service that allows the exchange of short text messages (up to 160 characters) between mobile devices over cellular networks.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refer to the RJ11 connector? (Select 3 answers)
questions.explanation: RJ11 (Registered Jack 11) is a smaller telephone connector with 4 or 6 pins, commonly used for telephone equipment, dial-up networking, and connections using twisted-pair copper cabling.

questions.stem: What is the most common memory module form factor used in laptops?
questions.explanation: SODIMM (Small Outline Dual In-Line Memory Module) is a compact memory module form factor designed for laptops and other space-constrained devices, roughly half the size of a standard desktop DIMM.

questions.stem: The backlight technology most commonly used in modern laptops is called:
questions.explanation: LED (Light-Emitting Diode) is a semiconductor-based light source widely used as the backlight technology in modern laptop and desktop displays, offering improved brightness, thinner profiles, and better energy efficiency compared to older CCFL backlights.

questions.stem: For a wireless client to be able to connect to a network, the security type (e.g., WEP, WPA, WPA2, or WPA3) and encryption type (e.g., TKIP or AES) settings on the connecting host must match the corresponding wireless security settings on a WAP.
questions.explanation: WPA3 (Wi-Fi Protected Access 3) is the latest wireless security standard. For a wireless client to connect to a network, the security type (WEP, WPA, WPA2, or WPA3) and passphrase configured on the client must match the wireless access point's settings.

questions.stem: Which of the following terms refers to a network security solution providing a single point of protection against various types of threats?
questions.explanation: UTM (Unified Threat Management) is an all-in-one network security appliance that consolidates multiple security functions—such as firewall, intrusion detection/prevention, antivirus, content filtering, and VPN—into a single device.

questions.stem: Which of the MS Windows features allows users to run programs with the security privileges of another user?
questions.explanation: UAC (User Account Control) is a Windows security feature that prevents unauthorized changes to the operating system by prompting users for administrator approval before allowing actions that require elevated privileges.

questions.stem: Which of the acronyms listed below refers to software that provides the functionality of a physical computer?
questions.explanation: VM (Virtual Machine) is a software-based emulation of a physical computer that runs its own operating system and applications, isolated from the host system, created and managed by a hypervisor.

questions.stem: What are the characteristic features of the RJ45 connector? (Select 2 answers)
questions.explanation: RJ45 (Registered Jack 45) is an 8-pin connector commonly used for Ethernet network cabling with twisted-pair copper cables (such as Cat5e, Cat6, and Cat6a) to connect devices to a LAN.

questions.stem: Which type of memory is specifically designed to store image and video data for fast access by the graphics processor?
questions.explanation: VRAM (Video Random Access Memory) is a specialized high-speed memory dedicated to storing image and video data for rapid access by the GPU, directly affecting graphics rendering performance and display resolution capabilities.

questions.stem: Which of the following answers refers to a software- or hardware-based security solution designed to detect and prevent the unauthorized use or transmission of confidential information?
questions.explanation: DLP (Data Loss Prevention) is a security strategy and set of software or hardware solutions designed to detect and prevent unauthorized access, use, or transmission of sensitive data outside an organization.

questions.stem: A specialized electronic component that accelerates visual rendering is referred to as:
questions.explanation: GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) is a specialized electronic processor designed to accelerate the rendering of images, video, and visual effects by performing rapid parallel mathematical calculations.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a network protocol used for synchronizing clocks over a computer network?
questions.explanation: NTP (Network Time Protocol) is a networking protocol used to synchronize the clocks of computers and devices across a network to a reference time source, ensuring accurate and consistent timekeeping.

questions.stem: SMB is a protocol used for:
questions.explanation: SMB (Server Message Block) is a network protocol used for sharing files, printers, and other resources between devices on a local network, primarily in Windows environments.
options: File and printer sharing between devices on a network
Collecting diagnostic and monitoring data from networked devices
Routing network traffic between different subnets
Managing and allocating IP addresses within a network
correctAnswer: File and printer sharing between devices on a network

questions.stem: Which of the following acronyms refers to a Microsoft-developed file system that provides advanced features including file and folder permissions, encryption, compression, and the ability to handle very large files and partitions?
questions.explanation: NTFS (New Technology File System) is a Microsoft-developed file system that provides advanced features including file-level security permissions, encryption (EFS), compression, disk quotas, and support for large volumes and files.

questions.stem: In the AAA security architecture, the process of granting or denying access to resources is known as:
questions.explanation: In the AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting) security framework, Authorization is the process of determining what resources and operations an authenticated user is permitted to access or perform.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a solution that allows network administrators to prioritize certain types of network traffic?
questions.explanation: QoS (Quality of Service) is a set of networking technologies and mechanisms that allow administrators to prioritize certain types of network traffic (such as voice or video) to ensure reliable performance and minimize latency.

questions.stem: What is the function of POP3?
questions.explanation: POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3) is an email retrieval protocol that downloads messages from a mail server to a local client, typically removing them from the server after download.

questions.stem: Which of the following acronyms refers to a short-range wireless communication technology used for contactless payments and data exchange?
questions.explanation: NFC (Near Field Communication) is a short-range wireless communication technology (typically within 4 cm) used for contactless payments, data sharing, and device pairing between NFC-enabled devices.

questions.stem: UDP is an example of a connectionless protocol. Because UDP does not support three-way handshake while establishing a network connection, it is referred to as unreliable or best-effort protocol. Example applications of UDP include transmission of video and audio streaming data.
questions.explanation: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is a connectionless transport layer protocol that does not use a three-way handshake, making it faster but less reliable than TCP. It is commonly used for real-time applications such as streaming, VoIP, and online gaming.

questions.stem: A networking hardware device connecting wireless devices to a wired network is referred to as:
questions.explanation: AP (Access Point) is a networking hardware device that connects wireless client devices to a wired network, acting as a bridge between Wi-Fi-enabled devices and the wired LAN infrastructure.

questions.stem: Which of the terms listed below refers to a product's life-cycle management phase in which a product is no longer being produced or sold?
questions.explanation: EOL (End of Life) is a product lifecycle phase in which a manufacturer ceases production, marketing, and sales of a product, often followed by a defined period of continued support before reaching end-of-support status.

questions.stem: What is a PUP? (Select 3 answers)
questions.explanation: PUP (Potentially Unwanted Program) is software that may not be explicitly classified as malware by antivirus software but can negatively affect system security and performance, compromise user privacy, or display unsolicited advertisements. PUPs are often bundled with other software and installed without fully informed user consent.
options: A type of computer program not explicitly classified as malware by AV software
An application downloaded and installed without the user's consent (illegal app)
A type of software that may adversely affect the computer's security and performance, compromise user's privacy, or display unsolicited ads
An application downloaded and installed with the user's consent, but often without fully informed agreement (typically bundled with other software)
A type of computer program explicitly classified as malware by AV applications
A type of free, utility software often bundled with a paid app
correctAnswer: A type of computer program not explicitly classified as malware by AV software
A type of software that may adversely affect the computer's security and performance, compromise user's privacy, or display unsolicited ads
An application downloaded and installed with the user's consent, but often without fully informed agreement (typically bundled with other software)

questions.stem: Which metric might be of help in diagnosing the declining performance of a storage drive?
questions.explanation: IOPS (Input/Output Operations Per Second) is a performance metric that measures how many read/write operations a storage device can perform per second, useful for diagnosing and benchmarking storage drive performance.

questions.stem: Which of the following answers refers to a computer's hardware component designed for enabling network access?
questions.explanation: NIC (Network Interface Card/Controller) is a hardware component that enables a computer to connect to and communicate over a network, whether through wired Ethernet or wireless Wi-Fi connections.

questions.stem: Which type of software allows centralized control over the configuration, monitoring, and security of mobile devices used within an organization?
questions.explanation: MDM (Mobile Device Management) is software that allows IT administrators to centrally configure, monitor, secure, and manage mobile devices (smartphones, tablets, laptops) used within an organization.

questions.stem: A type of network consisting of computers and peripheral devices that use high-frequency radio waves to communicate with each other is known as:
questions.explanation: WLAN (Wireless Local Area Network) is a type of local area network that uses high-frequency radio waves (Wi-Fi) instead of physical cables to connect computers and peripheral devices within a limited area.

questions.stem: Which of the terms listed below refers to a cloud computing service model in which clients, instead of buying all the hardware and software, purchase computing resources as an outsourced service from suppliers who own and maintain all the necessary equipment and software?
questions.explanation: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) is a cloud computing service model in which clients rent virtualized computing infrastructure—such as servers, storage, and networking—from a cloud provider instead of purchasing and maintaining their own physical hardware.

questions.stem: A Microsoft-proprietary protocol providing a user with graphical interface for connecting to another networked host is called:
questions.explanation: RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) is a Microsoft-proprietary protocol that provides a graphical interface for remotely connecting to and controlling another computer over a network.

questions.stem: Which WAN technology takes advantage of cell towers that provide wireless signal coverage for mobile devices?
questions.explanation: WWAN (Wireless Wide Area Network) is a wide area network technology that uses cellular tower infrastructure to provide wireless signal coverage for mobile devices over large geographic areas, utilizing standards like 4G LTE and 5G.

questions.stem: Which of the following answers refers to an analog video interface standard commonly used for connecting computer monitors before digital connections?
questions.explanation: VGA (Video Graphics Array) is a legacy analog video interface standard originally developed by IBM, commonly used for connecting monitors to computers via a 15-pin D-sub connector.

questions.stem: Which technology uses biometric data to identify or verify a person based on their facial features?
questions.explanation: FRT (Facial Recognition Technology) uses biometric data to identify or verify a person's identity by analyzing and comparing their facial features against stored reference images or templates.

questions.stem: An MS Windows stop error is informally referred to as:
questions.explanation: BSoD (Blue Screen of Death) is the informal name for a Windows stop error screen, displayed when the operating system encounters a critical error from which it cannot safely recover, requiring a system restart.

questions.stem: Which of the acronyms listed below refers to a security standard introduced to address the vulnerabilities found in WEP?
questions.explanation: WPA (Wi-Fi Protected Access) is a wireless security standard introduced as an interim improvement over WEP (Wired Equivalent Privacy), addressing its significant encryption vulnerabilities with stronger TKIP-based encryption.

questions.stem: ECC type RAM:
questions.explanation: ECC (Error-Correcting Code) RAM is a type of memory that can detect and automatically correct single-bit data errors, providing increased data integrity and reliability for servers and workstations running critical applications.
options: Can only detect errors, but does not have the capability to correct them
Refers to parity RAM (the two terms are interchangeable)
Offers better performance in terms of speed when compared to a non-ECC type of RAM

questions.stem: Which of the following terms refers to a global standard development organization composed of different national standards bodies?
questions.explanation: ISO (International Organization for Standardization) is a global body composed of representatives from national standards organizations that develops and publishes international standards across various industries and technologies.

questions.stem: A dedicated local network consisting of devices providing data access is known as:
questions.explanation: SAN (Storage Area Network) is a dedicated high-speed network that provides block-level access to consolidated data storage, connecting servers to shared storage devices for improved performance and centralized management.

questions.stem: As opposed to the simple DoS attacks that usually are performed from a single system, a DDoS attack uses multiple compromised computer systems to perform the attack against its target.
questions.explanation: DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) is an attack that uses multiple compromised systems (often a botnet) to flood a target with overwhelming traffic, unlike a simple DoS attack which originates from a single source.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a dedicated programming language used in database management?
questions.explanation: SQL (Structured Query Language) is a dedicated programming language used for managing, querying, and manipulating data stored in relational database management systems (RDBMS).

questions.stem: A system that uses a public network (such as the Internet) as a means for creating private encrypted connections between remote locations is called:
questions.explanation: VPN (Virtual Private Network) is a technology that creates an encrypted tunnel over a public network (such as the Internet) to securely connect remote users or sites to a private network, protecting data confidentiality and integrity.

questions.stem: The SMTP protocol is used for: (Select 2 answers)
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is the standard protocol used for sending email messages between mail servers and from client devices to outgoing mail servers.
options: Sending email messages between mail servers
Retrieving email messages from mail servers
Sending email messages from a client device
correctAnswer: Sending email messages between mail servers
Sending email messages from a client device

questions.stem: An authentication subsystem that enables a user to access multiple, connected system components (such as separate hosts on a network) after a single login on only one of the components is referred to as:
questions.explanation: SSO (Single Sign-On) is an authentication mechanism that allows a user to log in once and gain access to multiple connected applications or systems without re-entering credentials for each one.

questions.stem: Which of the following answers refers to a file system developed by Apple for use in its operating systems?
questions.explanation: APFS (Apple File System) is a proprietary file system developed by Apple, optimized for flash and SSD storage, used across macOS, iOS, and other Apple operating systems.

questions.stem: A type of LAN used in small business environments is referred to as:
questions.explanation: SOHO (Small Office/Home Office) refers to a small-scale network environment typically found in small businesses or home offices, connecting a limited number of devices via a single router or switch.

questions.stem: Which cyberattack involves impersonating a legitimate business contact via email to trick employees into harmful actions such as transferring funds or sharing sensitive information?
questions.explanation: BEC (Business Email Compromise) is a cyberattack in which an attacker impersonates a trusted business contact via email to deceive employees into transferring funds, sharing credentials, or performing other harmful actions.

questions.stem: Which DVI connector type does not provide support for analog signal transmission?
questions.explanation: DVI-D (Digital Visual Interface – Digital) carries only digital video signals and does not support analog signal transmission, unlike DVI-I which supports both digital and analog.

questions.stem: Adding an eSATA device to a PC can be done either by attaching the device cable directly to the motherboard's integrated I/O panel, connecting it via eSATA port on a modular bracket mounted on the back of the PC case, or attaching it directly to a dedicated slot on the motherboard.
questions.explanation: eSATA (External Serial Advanced Technology Attachment) is an external SATA interface for connecting storage devices. The statement is false because eSATA devices connect via an external eSATA port (on the I/O panel or an expansion bracket), not directly to an internal motherboard slot.

questions.stem: Which of the acronyms listed below refers to a backup rotation scheme?
questions.explanation: GFS (Grandfather-Father-Son) is a common backup rotation scheme that organizes backups into three tiers — daily (son), weekly (father), and monthly (grandfather) — to balance data retention with efficient use of storage media.

questions.stem: A type of document stipulating rules of behavior to be followed by users of computers, networks, and associated resources is known as:
questions.explanation: AUP (Acceptable Use Policy) is a document that defines the rules and guidelines users must follow when accessing an organization's computers, networks, and associated resources.

questions.stem: What are the characteristic features of an OLED display? (Select 3 answers)
questions.explanation: OLED (Organic Light-Emitting Diode) is a display technology in which each pixel emits its own light, eliminating the need for a backlight. OLED displays offer superior contrast ratios and color reproduction compared to LCDs, but typically have lower maximum brightness.
options: Inferior contrast ratio and color representation in comparison to LCDs
Lower light output (brightness) in comparison to LCDs
Display type commonly used in modern laptop devices
Better contrast ratio and color representation in comparison to LCDs
Requires backlight to illuminate the screen
Lower cost in comparison to LCDs
Higher light output (brightness) in comparison to LCDs
correctAnswer: Lower light output (brightness) in comparison to LCDs
Better contrast ratio and color representation in comparison to LCDs

questions.stem: Which of the AAA solutions listed below relies on TCP, separates authentication, authorization, and accounting, and is commonly used for device administration in enterprise networks?
questions.explanation: TACACS+ (Terminal Access Controller Access-Control System Plus) is an AAA protocol that uses TCP, encrypts the entire packet payload, and separates authentication, authorization, and accounting functions — making it well-suited for device administration in enterprise networks.

questions.stem: What is the function of a DNS TXT record? (Select 2 answers)
questions.explanation: A DNS TXT (Domain Name System Text) record stores arbitrary text-based data associated with a domain, commonly used for email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and domain ownership verification. TXT records do not direct any network traffic.
options: Resolves an IP address to a hostname for reverse lookups
Maps a domain name to a list of mail servers for that domain
Used to store text-based data associated with a domain
Not used to direct any traffic
Allows multiple domain names to resolve to the same IP address
correctAnswer: Used to store text-based data associated with a domain
Not used to direct any traffic

questions.stem: A type of ISP offering Internet access to subscribers at a designated wireless hotspot is called:
questions.explanation: WISP (Wireless Internet Service Provider) is a type of ISP that delivers Internet connectivity to subscribers via wireless links, typically at designated hotspot locations or through fixed wireless access points.

questions.stem: Which of the following answers refers to the diagnostic test a computer performs immediately after powering on to check hardware functionality?
questions.explanation: POST (Power-On Self-Test) is a diagnostic process that a computer's firmware (BIOS/UEFI) performs immediately after powering on to verify that essential hardware components such as the CPU, RAM, and storage are functioning correctly.

questions.stem: Which DVI connector type does not provide support for digital signal transmission?
questions.explanation: DVI-A (Digital Visual Interface – Analog) carries only analog video signals and does not support digital signal transmission, functioning similarly to a VGA connection through the DVI form factor.

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics describe the LC fiber-optic connector? (Select 3 answers)
questions.explanation: LC (Lucent Connector) is a small form factor fiber-optic connector that uses a latch locking mechanism similar to RJ-45 connectors. Its compact size makes it ideal for high-density network environments such as data centers.
options: Common in older networks and multimode fiber setups
Latch locking mechanism similar to RJ-45 connectors
Common in high-density network environments like data centers
correctAnswer: Latch locking mechanism similar to RJ-45 connectors
Common in high-density network environments like data centers

questions.stem: What are the characteristic features of IPS? (Select 3 answers)
questions.explanation: IPS (In-Plane Switching) is an LCD panel technology known for its high color accuracy and wide viewing angles. However, IPS panels typically have slower response times compared to TN panels, making them less ideal for fast-paced gaming.

questions.stem: A rule-based access control mechanism implemented on routers, switches, and firewalls is referred to as:
questions.explanation: ACL (Access Control List) is a rule-based access control mechanism used on routers, switches, and firewalls to permit or deny network traffic based on defined criteria such as IP addresses, ports, and protocols.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a set of parallel interface standards designed for connecting peripheral devices?
questions.explanation: SCSI (Small Computer System Interface) is a set of parallel interface standards originally designed for connecting peripheral devices such as hard drives, tape drives, and scanners to computers.

questions.stem: Which of the following terms describes the remote delivery of a wide range of computing services, including software, platforms, and infrastructure?
questions.explanation: XaaS (Anything as a Service) is a broad cloud computing term describing the remote delivery of virtually any computing service — including software, platforms, infrastructure, and more — over the Internet on a subscription or pay-per-use basis.

questions.stem: A mobile device's built-in functionality enabling the usage of locator applications is known as:
questions.explanation: GPS (Global Positioning System) is a satellite-based navigation system built into mobile devices that enables location tracking, mapping, and navigation through locator applications.

questions.stem: The DVI-I connector type provides support for both digital and analog video signal transmission.
questions.explanation: DVI-I (Digital Visual Interface – Integrated) is a connector type that supports both digital and analog video signal transmission, combining the capabilities of DVI-D (digital) and DVI-A (analog) in a single connector.

questions.stem: Which of the acronyms listed below refers to a page description language developed to control printer features and manage document printing?
questions.explanation: PCL (Printer Command Language) is a page description language developed by Hewlett-Packard to control printer features, format pages, and manage document printing across a wide range of printer models.

questions.stem: Which type of RAM features separate electrical contacts on each side of the module?
questions.explanation: DIMM (Dual Inline Memory Module) is a type of RAM module that features separate electrical contacts on each side of the circuit board, effectively doubling the data path width compared to older SIMM modules.

questions.stem: A computer network connecting multiple smaller networks over very large geographical areas is called:
questions.explanation: WAN (Wide Area Network) is a type of computer network that spans large geographical areas, connecting multiple smaller networks (such as LANs) across cities, countries, or continents — the Internet being the largest example.

questions.stem: A network admin can ping remote host by its IP address, but not by its domain name. Which of the following is the most probable source of this problem?
questions.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses. If a host can be reached by IP address but not by domain name, the problem most likely lies with the DNS server or DNS configuration.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refer to IMAP? (Select 2 answers)
questions.explanation: IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) is an email retrieval protocol that serves the same function as POP3 — retrieving email from a mail server — but offers improved functionality including server-side message storage, folder management, and multi-device synchronization.
options: Offers improved functionality in comparison to POP3
Serves the same function as POP3
Enables sending email messages from client devices
Enables email exchange between mail servers
correctAnswer: Offers improved functionality in comparison to POP3
Serves the same function as POP3

questions.stem: Which of the following answers describe characteristic features of DSL? (Select 3 answers)
questions.explanation: DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) is a family of broadband Internet access technologies that transmit data over existing copper telephone lines. DSL is commonly used as a last-mile solution to connect subscribers to their ISP.

questions.stem: An agreement granting the right to use a software application in a manner determined by the software vendor is referred to as:
questions.explanation: EULA (End-User License Agreement) is a legal contract between a software vendor and the end user that grants the right to use the software application under specific terms and conditions defined by the vendor.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a secure replacement for Telnet?
questions.explanation: SSH (Secure Shell) is a cryptographic network protocol that provides encrypted remote command-line access to network devices and servers, serving as a secure replacement for the unencrypted Telnet protocol.

questions.stem: Which DNS database record type allows multiple domain names to resolve to the same IP address?
questions.explanation: CNAME (Canonical Name) is a DNS record type that creates an alias mapping one domain name to another, allowing multiple domain names to resolve to the same IP address without requiring separate A records for each.

questions.stem: Which of the following file systems is known for its 4 GB maximum file size and 2 TB maximum volume size limitations?
questions.explanation: FAT32 (File Allocation Table 32-bit) is a widely compatible file system known for its limitations of a 4 GB maximum individual file size and a 2 TB maximum volume size, making it unsuitable for large modern files.

questions.stem: What are the characteristics of GPT? (Select 3 answers)
questions.explanation: GPT (GUID Partition Table) is a modern disk partitioning scheme associated with UEFI firmware that supports disks larger than 2 TB, allows up to 128 primary partitions, and provides built-in redundancy for partition table data.
options: Support for disks larger than 2 TB
Overall number of partitions limited to 4
Maximum disk size limit of 2 TB
correctAnswer: Support for disks larger than 2 TB

questions.stem: Which of the acronyms listed below refers to a unique string of characters used to identify hardware, software, and data?
questions.explanation: GUID (Globally Unique Identifier) is a 128-bit unique reference string used to identify hardware, software, partitions, and other data objects, ensuring each item has a distinct identity across systems.

questions.stem: An agreement between a service provider and users defining the nature, availability, quality, and scope of the service to be provided is known as:
questions.explanation: SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a formal agreement between a service provider and its users that defines the expected nature, availability, quality, and scope of the service, including metrics and remedies for non-compliance.

questions.stem: Which of the following terms refers to a solution used for authentication, authorization, and user identity management within an organization?
questions.explanation: IAM (Identity and Access Management) is a framework of policies, technologies, and processes used for managing digital identities and controlling user access to organizational resources through authentication and authorization.

questions.stem: IPS, TN, VA, and OLED are all implementations of LCD display technology.
questions.explanation: IPS (In-Plane Switching), TN (Twisted Nematic), and VA (Vertical Alignment) are all LCD panel technologies, but OLED (Organic Light-Emitting Diode) is a fundamentally different display technology that does not use liquid crystals — making the statement false.

questions.stem: Which type of fiber-optic equipment can be found at a demarc?
questions.explanation: ONT (Optical Network Terminal) is a fiber-optic device installed at the demarcation point (demarc) that converts optical signals from the ISP's fiber network into electrical signals usable by the customer's network equipment.

questions.stem: What are the characteristic features of the BNC connector? (Select 3 answers)
questions.explanation: BNC (Bayonet Neill–Concelman) is a coaxial cable connector featuring a bayonet-style twist-and-lock coupling mechanism, commonly used in professional audio/video equipment, CCTV systems, and laboratory testing equipment.
options: Professional audio and video equipment, CCTV systems, laboratory, and testing equipment
Satellite/cable TV, broadband Internet connections via cable modems
correctAnswer: Professional audio and video equipment, CCTV systems, laboratory, and testing equipment

questions.stem: A device designed to provide emergency power during an unexpected main power source outage is called:
questions.explanation: UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) is a device that provides emergency battery backup power during unexpected main power outages, protecting connected equipment from data loss and hardware damage.

questions.stem: In GPT disk architecture, each partition is labeled with a unique identifier known as GUID.
questions.explanation: In GPT (GUID Partition Table) disk architecture, each partition is assigned a unique GUID (Globally Unique Identifier), ensuring every partition can be distinctly identified regardless of the system or configuration.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a proprietary line of low-power, small form factor motherboards designed for industrial and embedded PC applications?
questions.explanation: ITX (Information Technology eXtended) refers to a family of small form factor motherboard standards developed by VIA Technologies, designed for low-power, compact, and embedded PC applications such as industrial systems and thin clients.

questions.stem: A type of control access technology providing protection against copyright infringements is referred to as:
questions.explanation: DRM (Digital Rights Management) is a set of access control technologies used to restrict the use, modification, and distribution of copyrighted digital content such as software, music, movies, and ebooks.

questions.stem: Which of the following acronyms refers to a security vulnerability that allows attackers to inject malicious scripts into web pages viewed by other users?
questions.explanation: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) is a web security vulnerability that allows attackers to inject malicious scripts into web pages viewed by other users, potentially stealing session cookies, credentials, or other sensitive data.

questions.stem: Which AAA solution uses UDP as its transport protocol, combines authentication and authorization, and is commonly deployed for network access control such as VPNs and Wi-Fi authentication?
questions.explanation: RADIUS (Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service) is an AAA protocol that uses UDP as its transport, combines authentication and authorization into a single process, and is commonly deployed for network access control including VPN and Wi-Fi authentication.

questions.stem: Which of the terms listed below best applies to the authentication process?
questions.explanation: MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication) is a security mechanism that requires users to verify their identity using two or more distinct authentication factors — such as something you know, something you have, and something you are.

questions.stem: A Microsoft-proprietary file system optimized for flash drives is known as:
questions.explanation: exFAT (Extensible File Allocation Table) is a Microsoft-proprietary file system optimized for flash storage devices such as USB drives and SD cards, supporting large file sizes without the 4 GB limitation of FAT32.

questions.stem: What are the characteristic features of SMB/CIFS? (Select 2 answers)
questions.explanation: SMB/CIFS (Server Message Block / Common Internet File System) is a network file-sharing protocol primarily used in Microsoft Windows environments to provide shared access to files, directories, printers, and other network resources.
options: Optimized for secure file sharing over the Internet
Primarily used in Microsoft Windows environments
Used to provide shared access to files, directories, and devices
Intended for voice and multimedia communication over IP networks
correctAnswer: Primarily used in Microsoft Windows environments
Used to provide shared access to files, directories, and devices

questions.stem: Which of the following answers refers to an older, portable device SSD form factor superseded by M.2?
questions.explanation: mSATA (Mini-SATA) is a compact SSD form factor designed for portable devices that uses a smaller physical connector than standard SATA. It has largely been superseded by the M.2 form factor, which offers greater flexibility and performance.

questions.stem: What are the characteristic features of the ST fiber-optic connector? (Select 3 answers)
questions.explanation: ST (Straight Tip) is a fiber-optic connector with a large cylindrical body and a bayonet twist-and-lock coupling mechanism. It is commonly found in older networks and multimode fiber installations.
options: Common in high-density network environments like data centers
Common in older networks and multimode fiber setups
Latch locking mechanism similar to RJ-45 connectors
correctAnswer: Common in older networks and multimode fiber setups

questions.stem: Which of the terms listed below refers to the concept of ephemeral access, where temporary code is used to verify user identity?
questions.explanation: OTP (One-Time Password) is a temporary, single-use code generated for a specific authentication session, providing ephemeral access that expires after one use or a short time period to enhance login security.

questions.stem: Which of the following acronyms refers to a document that outlines safety information, hazards, and handling instructions for chemicals or materials?
questions.explanation: MSDS (Material Safety Data Sheet) is a document that provides detailed safety information about chemicals or hazardous materials, including handling instructions, health hazards, first aid measures, and proper disposal procedures.

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics apply to the type of RAM most commonly used as the main system memory in desktop PCs? (Select 2 answers)
questions.explanation: Desktop PCs most commonly use DRAM (Dynamic Random-Access Memory) in non-ECC (non-Error Correcting Code) configuration. DRAM requires constant refreshing to retain data and is the standard for consumer desktops, while ECC memory is typically reserved for servers and workstations.

questions.stem: In older, non-UEFI-based PCs, the first sector of a storage drive containing information about partitions and a piece of executable code used to load the installed OS is referred to as:
questions.explanation: MBR (Master Boot Record) is the first sector of a storage drive in legacy BIOS-based systems, containing the partition table and a small piece of executable bootstrap code used to locate and load the installed operating system.

questions.stem: Which type of legal agreement involves a mutual obligation between parties to protect shared confidential information from unauthorized disclosure?
questions.explanation: NDA (Non-Disclosure Agreement) is a legal contract that creates a mutual or unilateral obligation between parties to protect shared confidential information from unauthorized disclosure to third parties.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below describe the SC fiber-optic connector? (Select 2 answers)
questions.explanation: SC (Subscriber Connector) is a fiber-optic connector featuring a push-pull locking mechanism for easy insertion and removal. It is widely used in both datacom and telecom applications due to its reliable connection and ease of use.
options: Widely used in datacom and telecom applications
Latch locking mechanism similar to RJ-45 connectors
Push-pull locking mechanism for easy insertion and removal
Common in older networks and multimode fiber setups
correctAnswer: Widely used in datacom and telecom applications
Push-pull locking mechanism for easy insertion and removal

questions.stem: Which non-proprietary remote-access protocol enables control over another computer on the network with the use of GUI?
questions.explanation: VNC (Virtual Network Computing) is a non-proprietary, platform-independent remote-access protocol that allows a user to view and control another computer's desktop over a network using a graphical user interface.

questions.stem: Which of the following acronyms refers to a video or display resolution standard that defines high- quality image resolutions, primarily in formats such as 720p and 1080p?
questions.explanation: HD (High Definition) refers to a video and display resolution standard that defines high-quality image formats, primarily 720p (1280×720) and 1080p (1920×1080), offering significantly more detail than standard definition (SD).

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to an API that enables communication between hosts on a LAN?
questions.explanation: NetBIOS (Network Basic Input/Output System) is a networking API that provides services for communication between applications on hosts within a local area network, enabling name resolution, session management, and data transfer.

questions.stem: The VA display technology can be characterized by: (Select 3 answers)
questions.explanation: VA (Vertical Alignment) is an LCD panel technology that offers high contrast ratios, good color reproduction, and good viewing angles, serving as a middle ground between the fast response times of TN panels and the wide viewing angles of IPS panels.

questions.stem: Which type of RAM transfers data on both the rising and falling edges of the clock signal?
questions.explanation: DDR (Double Data Rate) is a type of synchronous dynamic RAM that transfers data on both the rising and falling edges of the clock signal, effectively doubling the data throughput compared to single data rate (SDR) memory.

questions.stem: Which of the following terms refers to an embedded microcontroller used for secure boot, disk encryption, and system integrity verification?
questions.explanation: TPM (Trusted Platform Module) is a dedicated hardware microcontroller embedded on the motherboard that provides security functions such as secure boot verification, disk encryption key storage, and system integrity measurements.

questions.stem: Which of the acronyms listed below refers to the primary color model used in electronic displays, digital imaging, and screen-based color reproduction?
questions.explanation: RGB (Red, Green, Blue) is the primary additive color model used in electronic displays, digital imaging, and screen-based color reproduction, where varying intensities of red, green, and blue light are combined to produce a wide spectrum of colors.

questions.stem: A type of customizable framework providing access to a collection of system tools designed to manage networks, computers, services, and other system components in MS Windows is known as:
questions.explanation: MMC (Microsoft Management Console) is a customizable framework in Windows that hosts administrative snap-in tools for managing networks, computers, services, and other system components through a unified graphical interface.

questions.stem: Which of the following refers to a Microsoft file system specifically designed for maximum resilience, data integrity, and large-scale storage deployments in enterprise environments?
questions.explanation: ReFS (Resilient File System) is a Microsoft file system designed for maximum data integrity, automatic error correction, and scalability in enterprise-grade storage environments, serving as a complement to NTFS for large-scale deployments.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft protocol enables remote command-line management and automation of tasks on Windows-based systems?
questions.explanation: WinRM (Windows Remote Management) is a Microsoft protocol that enables remote command-line management and automation of tasks on Windows systems, using the WS-Management standard for communication between local and remote computers.

questions.stem: Which of the terms listed below refers to a high-speed serial interface designed specifically for connecting enterprise storage?
questions.explanation: SAS (Serial Attached SCSI) is a high-speed serial interface designed primarily for connecting enterprise-grade storage devices, offering higher reliability, faster data transfer rates, and support for longer cables compared to consumer-level SATA.

questions.stem: Which cybersecurity service offers continuous monitoring, threat detection, and response, typically managed by a third party to protect an organization from advanced threats?
questions.explanation: MDR (Managed Detection and Response) is a cybersecurity service that provides continuous monitoring, advanced threat detection, and incident response capabilities, typically delivered by a third-party provider to protect organizations from sophisticated threats.

questions.stem: Which acronym refers to the management of users with elevated privileges on critical systems?
questions.explanation: PAM (Privileged Access Management) is a security framework focused on managing, monitoring, and securing accounts with elevated privileges on critical systems to prevent unauthorized access and reduce the risk of insider threats.

questions.stem: Which of the following answers refers to hardware, often accompanied by software or firmware, designed to provide cryptographic key management and encryption functions?
questions.explanation: HSM (Hardware Security Module) is a dedicated physical device designed to manage cryptographic keys, perform encryption and decryption operations, and provide tamper-resistant secure storage for sensitive key material.

questions.stem: Which acronym refers to a common interface for connecting consumer-level storage devices like hard drives and SSDs?
questions.explanation: SATA (Serial Advanced Technology Attachment) is a standard serial interface widely used for connecting consumer-level storage devices such as hard drives, SSDs, and optical drives to a computer's motherboard.

questions.stem: What is the name of a policy framework that allows domain owners to specify how email receivers should handle emails that fail authentication checks?
questions.explanation: DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) is an email authentication policy framework that allows domain owners to specify how receiving mail servers should handle messages that fail SPF or DKIM authentication checks.

questions.stem: An authentication mechanism that generates one-time passwords based on the current time and a secret key is called:
questions.explanation: TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) is an authentication algorithm that generates temporary one-time passwords using the current time and a shared secret key, providing a constantly rotating code typically valid for 30-60 seconds.

questions.stem: Which of the terms listed below refers to a high-performance file system commonly used in UNIX- like operating systems such as Linux to handle very large files and storage volumes?
questions.explanation: XFS (eXtended File System) is a high-performance 64-bit journaling file system commonly used in UNIX-like operating systems such as Linux, designed to handle very large files and storage volumes efficiently.

questions.stem: What is the name of a DNS TXT record that allows the owner of a domain to specify all the servers authorized to send mail from their domain?
questions.explanation: SPF (Sender Policy Framework) is a DNS TXT record-based email authentication method that allows domain owners to specify which mail servers are authorized to send email on behalf of their domain, helping to prevent email spoofing.

questions.stem: Which of the following answers refers to a serial communication copper connector often found on older PCs, networking equipment, and industrial hardware?
questions.explanation: DB-9 (D-subminiature 9-pin) is a serial communication connector commonly found on older PCs and networking equipment, historically used for RS-232 serial connections to devices such as modems, routers, and console ports.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refer to valid examples of items tracked in a CMDB? (Select 2 answers)
questions.explanation: CMDB (Configuration Management Database) is a centralized repository used in IT service management to track and store information about configuration items (CIs) such as server hardware, installed applications, network devices, and their relationships.

questions.stem: Which of the following wireless encryption protocols was introduced with WPA to replace WEP?
questions.explanation: TKIP (Temporal Key Integrity Protocol) is a wireless encryption protocol introduced with WPA (Wi-Fi Protected Access) as a more secure replacement for the vulnerable WEP protocol, providing per-packet key mixing and message integrity checks.

questions.stem: A type of architecture that simplifies networking by allowing devices to dynamically join a network, autoconfigure, and learn about the presence and capabilities of other devices is referred to as:
questions.explanation: UPnP (Universal Plug and Play) is a set of networking protocols that allows devices to dynamically discover each other, join a network, autoconfigure network settings, and advertise their capabilities without manual configuration.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a non-volatile mass storage media type that uses flash memory and has no moving parts, offering faster access than spinning disk drives?
questions.explanation: SSD (Solid-State Drive) is a non-volatile mass storage device that uses flash memory (NAND) chips to store data, offering significantly faster read/write speeds, lower latency, and greater durability than traditional HDDs since it has no moving mechanical parts.

questions.stem: Which of the following answers refer(s) to ARM-type CPU architecture? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: ARM (Advanced RISC Machine) is a CPU architecture based on reduced instruction set computing (RISC) principles, characterized by low power consumption, simplified instruction sets, and high efficiency — making it the dominant architecture in mobile devices, embedded systems, and battery-powered devices.
options: Typically used in personal computers, laptops, and servers
Focuses on simplifying the instruction set to enhance processing efficiency
Employs complex instructions for efficient memory management and backward compatibility
Commonly used in mobile devices and embedded systems
correctAnswer: Focuses on simplifying the instruction set to enhance processing efficiency
Commonly used in mobile devices and embedded systems

questions.stem: Which of the terms listed below refer to SSD form factors? (Select 2 answers)
questions.explanation: M.2 and mSATA (Mini-SATA) are both SSD form factors. M.2 is the current standard supporting both SATA and NVMe interfaces in a compact card-like design, while mSATA is an older, smaller form factor that has been largely replaced by M.2.

questions.stem: Which of the following systems is specifically designed for remote, wide-area monitoring and supervisory control of industrial processes across multiple geographically dispersed sites?
questions.explanation: SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) is an industrial control system designed for remote, wide-area monitoring and supervisory control of geographically dispersed infrastructure such as power grids, pipelines, and water treatment facilities.

questions.stem: What is the name of an authentication method that enables the signing of an outbound email message with a digital signature?
questions.explanation: DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) is an email authentication method that allows the sending mail server to digitally sign outbound messages, enabling the recipient's server to verify the message's authenticity and integrity.

questions.stem: Which of the acronyms listed below refers to a security solution that provides the capability for detection, analysis, response, and real-time monitoring of cyber threats at the device level?
questions.explanation: EDR (Endpoint Detection and Response) is a security solution that continuously monitors endpoint devices to detect, analyze, and respond to cyber threats, providing real-time visibility into suspicious activities and automated remediation capabilities.

questions.stem: What are the characteristic features of the TN display technology? (Select 3 answers)
questions.explanation: TN (Twisted Nematic) is an LCD panel technology characterized by fast response times but limited viewing angles and lower color accuracy compared to IPS and VA panels, making it popular for budget monitors and competitive gaming displays.

questions.stem: A logical device interface used for accessing non-volatile memory storage devices attached via PCIe is known as:
questions.explanation: NVMe (Non-Volatile Memory Express) is a high-performance logical device interface and protocol designed specifically for accessing non-volatile flash storage devices connected via the PCIe bus, delivering significantly lower latency and higher throughput than SATA-based protocols.

questions.stem: Which of the following provides granular control over user access to specific network segments and resources based on their assigned roles and permissions?
questions.explanation: IAM (Identity and Access Management) provides granular control over user access to specific network segments and resources based on verified identity, roles, and policies, ensuring that only authorized users can reach sensitive systems.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to virtualization platform for delivering virtual desktops to a community of users?
questions.explanation: VDI (Virtual Desktop Infrastructure) is a virtualization technology that hosts and delivers virtual desktop environments from a centralized server to end users, allowing a community of users to access their desktops remotely from any device.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes a CPU architecture focused on a simplified set of instructions to enhance speed and efficiency?
questions.explanation: RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) is a CPU architecture that uses a simplified set of instructions, enabling each instruction to execute in fewer clock cycles, which enhances processing speed and energy efficiency.

questions.stem: A type of USB connection method commonly used in modern mobile devices due to its reversible design, fast data transfer, and power capabilities is called:
questions.explanation: USB-C (Universal Serial Bus Type-C) is a modern, reversible USB connector commonly used in mobile devices, laptops, and peripherals, supporting fast data transfer, power delivery, and video output through a single compact, symmetrical port.

questions.stem: Which of the terms listed below refers to a smart card issued by the U.S. Department of Defense for secure identification, authentication, and access to both physical locations and information systems?
questions.explanation: CAC (Common Access Card) is a smart card issued by the U.S. Department of Defense that serves as the standard identification for military personnel and contractors, providing secure physical and logical access through embedded certificates and cryptographic keys.

questions.stem: Which of the following refers to a documented set of instructions designed to ensure consistent execution of routine tasks?
questions.explanation: SOP (Standard Operating Procedure) is a documented set of step-by-step instructions designed to ensure consistent and correct execution of routine tasks and operations within an organization.

questions.stem: Which acronym refers to a cybersecurity approach that combines data from multiple security tools to provide comprehensive threat detection and response across endpoints, networks, and cloud environments?
questions.explanation: XDR (Extended Detection and Response) is a cybersecurity approach that integrates and correlates data from multiple security tools and sources — including endpoints, networks, servers, and cloud workloads — to provide comprehensive threat detection and automated response.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to any type of information pertaining to an individual that can be used to uniquely identify that person?
questions.explanation: PII (Personally Identifiable Information) refers to any data that can be used to uniquely identify, contact, or locate an individual, such as Social Security numbers, full names, email addresses, or biometric records.

questions.stem: What is the name of a security feature used in Bluetooth device pairing?
questions.explanation: PIN (Personal Identification Number) is a numeric security code used during Bluetooth device pairing (and other authentication scenarios) to verify that both devices are authorized to establish a connection.

questions.stem: Which of the following enables operating system installation over a network interface?
questions.explanation: PXE (Preboot Execution Environment) is a standardized client-server framework that enables a computer to boot and install an operating system over a network interface, without requiring local storage media such as a hard drive or USB.

questions.stem: Which of the acronyms listed below refers to a markup language for exchanging authentication and authorization data?
questions.explanation: SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) is an XML-based markup language and open standard used for exchanging authentication and authorization data between identity providers and service providers, enabling single sign-on (SSO) functionality.

questions.stem: An Apple-exclusive mechanism for deploying time-sensitive security patches independently of major OS updates is referred to as:
questions.explanation: RSR (Rapid Security Response) is an Apple-exclusive mechanism that delivers time-sensitive security patches to macOS, iOS, and iPadOS devices independently of major OS updates, allowing critical vulnerabilities to be fixed quickly without a full system update.

questions.stem: Which of the following refers to a solution that allows IT professionals to remotely supervise and maintain client systems, including monitoring performance, deploying updates, and resolving issues without physical access?
questions.explanation: RMM (Remote Monitoring and Management) is a software solution that allows IT professionals to remotely supervise, maintain, and troubleshoot client systems and networks from a centralized console, enabling proactive support and patch management.

questions.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a standardized method employed by the U.S. federal government to authenticate the identities of employees and contractors via smart card-based credentials?
questions.explanation: PIV (Personal Identity Verification) is a standardized smart card-based credential used by the U.S. federal government to authenticate employees and contractors, providing secure physical and logical access to government systems and facilities.

questions.stem: Which of the following refers to a framework for evaluating and improving software development processes?
questions.explanation: SPICE (Software Process Improvement and Capability dEtermination) is an international framework (ISO/IEC 15504) for evaluating and improving software development processes by assessing process capability and organizational maturity.
